passage: Akash, not yet two, was usually all smiles. On Saturday in their Lucknow flat, he woke from his nap screaming. He pushed away his banana, clung to Avni's neck and kept rubbing one ear against her shoulder. That night he kept waking, crying whenever she laid him down. Avni sat up rocking him, watching his fist go back to that ear. "Something hurts, doesn't it?" she whispered. Next morning she took him to the paediatrician down the road.

qa.q: What did Akash push away?
qa.a: His banana.

qa.q: What was Akash feeling when he clung to Avni and rubbed his ear?
qa.a: He was in pain and frightened, and could only show it by crying, clinging and rubbing the ear.

qa.q: What did Avni do well in reading the signs?
qa.a: She noticed the sudden change in mood and the hand going back to his ear, guessed something hurt and took him to the paediatrician.

qa.q: What was the night like for Avni?
qa.a: Long and worrying; she sat up rocking him while he kept waking.

grounding: Shows a toddler who cannot name an ear pain showing it through crying, refusing food, clinging and broken sleep, with the mood change as the first clue.

passage:
"Zeenat won't eat anything," Sarika said, holding her dripping daughter.
Nani leaned in. "Look at her cheek. Red on one side. And all this drool."
Zeenat wailed and chewed hard on Sarika's thumb.
"Teeth," Nani said.
"She's so clingy. She screamed when I put her down."
"Try the cold teether from the fridge, and lots of cuddles."
Zeenat gnawed the teether, sobbing less.
"If it keeps going or worries you, check with the doctor," Nani said.

qa.q: What did Zeenat chew hard on?
qa.a: Sarika's thumb.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling when she screamed at being put down?
qa.a: She was sore and upset from her teeth, so she wanted to be held and felt safer close to Sarika.

qa.q: What helped, and what is the sensible next step if it goes on?
qa.a: A cold teether and cuddles helped; if it keeps going or worries them, checking with the doctor is the sensible step.

qa.q: How does Nani read Zeenat's mood?
qa.a: Nani sees the red cheek and drool and reads the fussing as teething pain rather than bad temper.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler with teething pain who cannot name it refusing food, clinging and crying, the mood change being the first clue.

passage: In their Pune flat, Ramesh had been a giggly eater all week. Tonight he pushed the dal-rice away, cried when Lokesh tried to lay him down, and kept tugging at his left ear. He clung to Lokesh's shirt and would not let go. "Something hurts, na?" Lokesh whispered, walking him up and down the hall. When the crying woke him again in the night, Lokesh rang the family doctor's clinic first thing, and they were in the waiting room by nine.

qa.q: Which ear did Ramesh keep tugging?
qa.a: His left ear.

qa.q: What does Ramesh's crying and clinging suggest?
qa.a: He is in pain and upset, probably frightened, but too little to say what hurts.

qa.q: What sensible step did Lokesh take?
qa.a: He treated the sudden change in mood as a clue that something hurt, comforted him, and took him to the family doctor in the morning.

qa.q: What might the night be like for Lokesh?
qa.a: Tiring and worrying, walking the hall with a crying child and waiting for morning.

grounding: Shows a toddler who cannot name an earache refusing food, clinging and crying, with the sudden mood change as the first clue.

passage:
"Shreya, what's wrong with him today? He threw his banana at me!"
"I don't know, Mummy. He bit my shoulder, and now he won't eat."
"Look at the drool. Chin all red, fist in his mouth."
"Ramesh, come here, baby. Let me see. There. Feel that, Mummy? A new tooth at the back."
"Ah. So that's the grumpy prince."
"No wonder he didn't sleep. His gums must hurt."
"Give him the cold teething ring from the fridge."
"Good idea. And if he's still this miserable tomorrow, I'll ask the doctor."

qa.q: What did Shreya feel at the back of Ramesh's mouth?
qa.a: A new tooth at the back.

qa.q: What was Ramesh feeling when he threw his banana?
qa.a: He was in pain and cranky from his sore gums, and too little to say so.

qa.q: What was sensible about Shreya's plan?
qa.a: She eased the pain with the cold teething ring and planned to ask the doctor if he stayed this miserable.

qa.q: How did Mummy first see Ramesh's mood?
qa.a: At first she saw only a grumpy child throwing food, until the drool and red chin pointed to teething.

grounding: Shows a teething toddler throwing food, biting and not sleeping, with the sudden mood change as the first clue that something hurts.

passage:
Daycare note for Swati's parents, Tuesday
Swati was not herself today. Usually she is first to the sandpit, but after lunch she refused her fruit, wanted to be held all the time, and cried whenever I put her down. She kept rubbing her right ear against my shoulder and slept only for a few minutes. I called you at 2 pm so you could collect her early, and you said you're taking her to the doctor this evening. Hoping the ear is better soon.
Dhruv

qa.q: Which ear did Swati keep rubbing?
qa.a: Her right ear.

qa.q: What was Swati feeling after lunch?
qa.a: She seemed uncomfortable and upset, wanting to be held because something hurt that she could not name.

qa.q: What did Dhruv do that helped?
qa.a: Dhruv noticed the sudden change in mood as a clue, kept her close, and called her parents the same day so she could see a doctor.

qa.q: How might Swati's parents feel reading the note?
qa.a: Worried but grateful that the change was noticed and they were called early.

grounding: Shows a toddler with ear pain refusing food, clinging and sleeping poorly, and a caregiver reading the mood change as the first clue.

passage: In the village near Moga, little Varun, usually happy chasing hens, cried all afternoon. He pushed away his roti, clung to Gurpreet's dupatta and woke screaming from his nap. Gurpreet's mother-in-law said, 'Spoilt, that's all.' But Gurpreet noticed him tugging at his right ear and turning his face into her shoulder. 'Something hurts,' she said. That evening she carried him to the health centre in the next village, where the doctor was still seeing patients. Varun slept on her shoulder all the way home.

qa.q: Which ear was Varun tugging?
qa.a: His right ear.

qa.q: What did Varun's crying and clinging suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He was in pain and upset but couldn't say it, so he cried, refused food and clung for comfort.

qa.q: Why was Gurpreet right to take Varun to the doctor?
qa.a: The sudden mood change and ear tugging were clues that something hurt, and a doctor could check it.

qa.q: How did the mother-in-law see Varun's crying?
qa.a: She saw a spoilt child, missing the signs that Varun was in pain.

grounding: A toddler with ear pain cannot name it and shows it through crying, refusing food and clinging.
